policies.title: Peerly Terms of Use
policies.content:
Peerly Terms of Use
Internal staging version: 2026-11-09

1. The service
Peerly helps APU Malaysia students find people to learn with and offer peer help. This staging deployment is intended for development-team and prototype testing. Features and availability may change while testing. Contact the Peerly development team at support@aleksei-orlov.dev.

2. Accounts and eligibility
Use your own Google identity and a student email address ending in @mail.apu.edu.my. Google sign-in and student-email verification are separate steps. Provide accurate information and keep access to your accounts secure. An institutional email check confirms access to that mailbox; it does not verify grades, enrolment in a particular module, expertise or the truth of profile statements.

3. Learning and contact
Knowledge areas and offers of help are self-declared. A topic, module code or course name supplies context; passing a named course is not a condition for helping with a related task. Review a person's profile and agree on the scope of help before relying on it. Follow your institution's assessment and academic-integrity rules. Peerly does not guarantee a match, response, qualification or learning outcome.

Requests and messages are governed by server-enforced limits, eligibility and pair state. Hiding a profile removes Discovery exposure and new contact but keeps existing conversations working. Blocking or moderation may restrict further interaction. Do not harass, impersonate, spam, misuse another person's data or bypass safeguards.

4. Your content
Upload and send only material you have the right to share. Do not share passwords, access tokens or unnecessary sensitive information. Profiles, messages, images, help declarations, goals, feedback and support submissions are stored as service records. You permit Peerly to store, process and display them to their intended participants and authorised operators for the purposes described in the Privacy Policy. You remain responsible for what you submit. Other participants may retain information you have already shared with them.

5. AI assistance
AI assistance is optional to use and may be unavailable, queued, delayed or rejected under load. It may help refine a goal, suggest a knowledge area or give advisory feedback on a photo. It can be incorrect and does not certify competence, decide punitive moderation or guarantee a useful result. Review suggestions before applying them. Applying a suggestion and publishing a goal are separate explicit actions. Keep using the manual path if AI is unavailable. AI processing and its providers are described in the Privacy Policy.

6. Safety and support
Use Report for a relevant profile, message or image, or contact support for access and service problems. A report does not automatically prove wrongdoing or block another user. Authorised operators may review retained records and restrict accounts. Support requests do not automatically change identity, restore a deleted account or bypass student verification. Support hours are 09:00–21:00 Malaysia time; a response-time guarantee is not provided.

7. Account deletion and retained history
Deleting your account disables access and revokes sessions. Other users see a deleted-account projection and retained conversation history; the operation does not erase everything previously shared. Peerly uses soft deletion: original account records, content, relationships, reports, audit records and linked analytics remain internally retained, subject to applicable obligations and the Privacy Policy. Private message text may itself contain identifying information and is not automatically rewritten. Normal sign-in does not recreate or restore a deleted account.

8. Analytics and operator access
Account-linked operational and product analytics are part of the service, without an in-app analytics opt-out. Authorised developers and operators can inspect retained business data and its links to activity, including private messages and media, under recorded access. Read the Privacy Policy before registering; it describes the data, purposes, retention and providers. This service agreement does not waive rights that cannot lawfully be waived.

9. Changes and availability
We may update these terms and the Privacy Policy. We will identify the published version and notify users of changes through the service or an available contact channel. A policy update does not normally require another acceptance screen; where applicable law requires a different process, that requirement takes precedence. Registration records refer to the versions actually shown at that time. Changes do not rewrite that historical record.

We may interrupt or change the prototype for maintenance, safety or capacity. No continuous-availability guarantee is made. Contact support@aleksei-orlov.dev about access, moderation, content or privacy concerns.

policies.title: Peerly Privacy Policy
policies.content:
Peerly Privacy Policy
Internal staging version: 2026-11-09

1. Who processes the data
The Peerly development team operates this service and handles privacy and support requests at support@aleksei-orlov.dev. This notice describes the internal staging service and the intended student features. It does not represent a guarantee that every external integration or monitoring component is already operational.

2. Data and sources
We process Google identity information needed for sign-in, your institutional email and verification state, account/session identifiers, registration-document versions and timestamps. We receive these from you, Google and service operations.

We store profile details, selected languages and knowledge areas, goals and task context, offers of help, profile photos, requests, chats and images, feedback, visibility/block/report choices and support submissions. Information may also come from people who message, report or review an interaction with you. Keep optional fields limited to information needed for the task.

When you explicitly use AI, we process the relevant submitted draft, selected context or image, the resulting task, output and execution status. A draft submitted to AI can be retained as a private task record even when you do not publish it as a goal.

We process network and browser/device information needed to deliver and secure requests, plus timestamps, account-linked product events, request/action identifiers, traces, service metrics, diagnostics and privileged-access audit records. We do not claim to record every keystroke or capture every technical event without loss.

3. Purposes and required data
Data is used for sign-in and membership verification, showing profiles and relevant partners, explicit requests and conversations, media processing, AI assistance, learning feedback, support, abuse prevention, debugging, service administration and product analysis. Required identity and setup data is necessary for the relevant account capabilities; optional profile details and optional AI use remain your choice.

Operational and product analytics are linked to your account and are a required part of using an account. There is no separate in-app analytics opt-out. This is distinct from optional notification preferences: security and verification messages remain necessary, while optional updates follow the saved preference and actual device/channel availability. If you do not wish to use an account under this model, do not register or stop using the service; this does not automatically remove earlier retained records.

4. Visibility and privileged inspection
Other users receive only the profile and interaction data that the applicable service rules authorise. Existing conversation participants can retain access to their conversation context even if a profile is hidden from Discovery. Deleted accounts use a deleted-account projection for other users; the underlying records are retained internally.

Authorised developers and operators have comprehensive access to retained accounts, profile revisions, messages, images, goals, help declarations, reports, support cases, AI tasks, relationships, activity and their links. This access can be used for service administration and investigation without an already open support case. Privileged inspection is audited. Ordinary users do not have access to internal Grafana or operator interfaces.

Private messages, images, support comments, AI text and credentials are not intended to be copied into ordinary application logs or technical metrics. Authoritative content stays in business storage and may be retrieved through privileged access when needed. Technical events use bounded metadata and identifiers to relate activity to the appropriate account and record.

5. Providers and processing locations
Current integration includes Google for identity, Brevo for transactional email, Cloud.ru for private object storage, and owner-managed PostgreSQL, application hosting and observability infrastructure. Product analytics uses the owner's Umami installation. AI tasks, when enabled and explicitly requested, use OpenAI through the dedicated Codex executor; the executor's subscription credentials are not user credentials. Email replies may pass through ImprovMX and the operator's receiving mailbox service.

These services and their infrastructure may process data outside Malaysia. The deployed provider/region inventory must be kept with the release record; request details through support@aleksei-orlov.dev. Enabling AI sends the task data required for that feature to the AI provider, not an automatic publication of your private conversation. Providers may process operational data under their own applicable terms and safeguards.

6. Retention and deletion
Account deletion is a soft-delete operation, not an instruction to erase every record. Peerly retains original account/content records, historical revisions, conversations/media, relationships, feedback, reports, support records, AI task records, audit and accumulated analytics internally after account access ends. These business records currently have no routine automatic expiry. Retention supports service history, integrity, support, safety and investigation and remains subject to applicable obligations and review.

Temporary upload transport, authentication challenges, credentials and delivery envelopes have separate security/cleanup lifetimes. Short-lived transport hints may be pruned without erasing the underlying business event. Diagnostic capture and archive availability depend on the actual deployed monitoring pipeline; an internal staging test is not a promise of permanent preservation of every log or trace.

Contact us about access, corrections, retention, deletion or objections to processing. We will review the request, confirm identity where appropriate and explain the outcome and any applicable retention or legal constraints. Agreement to this notice is not a waiver of rights that cannot lawfully be waived. An account-deletion button and a privacy request are separate processes.

7. Security and limitations
Access controls, private storage, session revocation, bounded execution and audit are used to protect the service. No system or prototype can guarantee absolute security, uninterrupted availability or perfect telemetry. Report a suspected security or privacy issue to support@aleksei-orlov.dev without including passwords or secret tokens.

8. Versions and updates
The service keeps versioned policy documents and the versions actually presented at registration. Updates are informational rather than an automatic reacceptance gate; where applicable obligations require an additional process, they take precedence. We will identify the changed version and notify users through the service or an available contact channel. Contact support@aleksei-orlov.dev for questions about this notice.
